name: SAINT LUCIA
lead: Saint Lucia is a volcanic island in the Caribbean. Two steep cones called the Pitons rise straight from the sea. Britain and France fought over it fourteen times. It has rainforest, reefs and banana farms.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Saint Lucia sits between the Caribbean Sea and the Atlantic. The twin Pitons, Gros Piton (770 m) and Petit Piton (743 m), are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Thick rainforest covers the inland, fed by 2,000 mm of rain a year. Sulphur Springs near Soufrière is the world's only drive-in volcano. You park beside bubbling grey mud.
animals: The Saint Lucia Parrot, or Jacquot, is bright green with red, blue and yellow markings. It lives nowhere else. Fewer than 150 survived in the 1970s. Now over 1,000 do.
Leatherback sea turtles, heavier than a motorbike, nest on the beaches each spring. Reefs shelter seahorses and flying fish. The frogfish disguises itself as a bumpy rock.
culture: Saint Lucians blend French, African and British traditions. The Creole language Kwéyòl sounds like French with a Caribbean twist. Its national day, Jounen Kwéyòl, comes every October with food and music.
Carnival bursts out each July with soca music and dazzling costumes. The national dish is green fig and saltfish. Cricket is practically a religion.
history: Arawak, then Carib, people lived here long before Europeans came. The harbour was a prize. Britain and France swapped control fourteen times between 1660 and 1814, a Caribbean record.
Enslaved Africans worked the sugar plantations. Their descendants form most of the population today. Slavery ended in 1834. Saint Lucia became fully independent on 22 February 1979.
wows: Two Nobel winners make Saint Lucia a world leader per person.
The Pitons are so famous that their shape alone says Saint Lucia.
At Sulphur Springs, you can drive within 20 m of boiling mud.
Parrot numbers grew from 150 in 1977 to over 1,000.
Saint Lucia changed rulers 14 times, leaving French and British marks.
Bananas grown in its volcanic soil taste sweeter than most.
The twin Pitons shelter Soufrière bay, giving calm sailing.

myths.fact: A banana plant is a giant herb with no wood. Its trunk is tightly wrapped leaves.
The leatherback's shell is soft and leathery, with no hard plates.
